paragraphs.source_en:
(‘Love, speaking fervently in my mind of my lady, often utters such things concerning her that my
intellect is bewildered by them. His speech sounds so sweetly that the soul, as she attends and hears,
says: “Alas that I am unable to express what I hear of my lady!” And certainly, if I wish to treat of what
I hear of her, I must first leave aside what my intellect does not grasp; and then, too, much of what it
does understand, for I should not be able to express it. If then these words of mine which undertake
her praise be found wanting, let the blame fall on the weak intellect, and on our faculty of speech
which lacks the power to record all that Love says.’ Trans. F&B)
